source_title: ‘Decide representation on Tribal Advisory Council appts’ - The Times of India
source_excerpt: Dehradun: Uttarakhand high court on Tuesday disposed of a PIL questioning the criteria for appointing and retaining members of the Uttarakhand Tribal Advisory Council, while granting the petitioner liberty to approach the competent authority with a formal representation. The authority will have to decide the representation within nine months after it is submitted.The PIL was filed by Bachna Sharma, who belongs to the Scheduled Tribe community. The petition questioned whether the integrity, public conduct and past contribution of council members towards the welfare of STs were being adequately considered under the existing framework.During the hearing, the petitioner argued that the Uttarakhand Tribal Advisory Council Rules, 2014, did not contain clear provisions requiring authorities to assess a memberâs integrity or record of work for the ST community. The petition relied on Section 4(2) of the Uttarakhand Scheduled Tribes Act, 2015, contending that such factors must be given due weight while making or reviewing appointments.The petition specifically referred to Geetaram Gaur, vice-chairman of the Uttarakhand Tribal Advisory Council, alleging that around 18 to 20 criminal cases and complaints were pending against him. The petitioner questioned whether a person facing such allegations should continue in a position involving responsibility for the interests and welfare of the tribal community.The allegations regarding the cases and complaints were placed before the court as part of the petitionerâs submissions. Their present status and merits remain subject to verification and determination by the competent authority on the basis of official records.After hearing the matter, HC permitted the petitioner to submit a representation to the competent authority within two weeks. It directed the authority to decide the representation within nine months, keeping in view Section 4(2) of the Uttarakhand Scheduled Tribes Act, 2015.Stay updated with the latest Dehradun news.
